messages:
jenna-sales: FYI customer POC failing during private/vpc test. They say inference calls to our hosted endpoint time out when routed through their NAT GW + proxy. Need quick triage and a shading note for pricing if we need Dedicated.
ryan-se: Can you paste the error they see? is it DNS or TLS? :thinking_face:
jenna-sales: They forwarded this from their dev:
jenna-sales: ```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate \n  --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.0.5.12 \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: TLSv1.2 (IN), TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake error
* curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
``` 
jenna-sales: They suspect TLS termination in a proxy chain, maybe SNI rewrite.
nina-sre: That curl suggests the client couldn't validate the cert chain. If they're routing through a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy that re-signs, we either need to trust their CA or bypass inspection for the endpoint.
arthur-infra: Also check PrivateLink vs Interface Endpoint DNS handing. If they enabled private DNS, their resolver should return our private endpoint IPs. If it returns the proxy IP, SNI mismatch happens.
jenna-sales: Customer says "we see the right private IPs" but our server logs show repeated handshake failures with same src IP. I asked for tcpdump but they shared a truncated log:
jenna-sales: ```
server tls: peer certificate signed by unknown authority; client_ip=10.0.5.12
server: TLS handshake aborted
``` 
ryan-se: Two paths: 1) have them allow passthrough to our endpoint (no MITM), 2) configure their proxy to forward original SNI and not terminate. Can we provide a short runbook they can hand to infra?
nina-sre: I'll draft steps. Quick checklist for them:
- Verify Route53 private hosted zone resolves api.redwood.example.com -> interface endpoint IPs
- Ensure security groups on the VPC endpoint allow 443 from the NAT+proxy IP range
- If TLS inspection is mandatory, add their CA to our mutual TLS trust is not possible; instead suggest allowing passthrough for Redwood endpoints
- Capture tcpdump on client side: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host api.redwood.example.com and port 443 -w /tmp/redwood.pcap`
arthur-infra: Also ask if their proxy rewrites Host header or SNI. Many proxies will SNIRemove/replace. If so, we can fallback to token-auth route on a different hostname they can whitelist.
jenna-sales: customer asks if there's an alternative host we can give that doesn't require private DNS (they have restrictive split-horizon rules).
nina-sre: We can offer a dedicated egress-friendly hostname in a public VPC for the POC (short-lived) but note this defeats private endpoint isolation. Prepare a pricing note: Dedicated endpoints or Dedicated capacity will be recommended if they need persistent high-throughput and isolated networking.
mark-sales: On pricing: if they move to Dedicated for guaranteed throughput and to avoid complex proxy handoffs, it's a committed monthly seat. I can send a ballpark: 3x hosted baseline for reserved capacity + setup. Will follow up via email.
jenna-sales: Customer also ran into intermittent 429s when they tried bypassing proxy for a short time. They said bursty calls during eval.
ryan-se: 429s likely rate limits from shared hosted pool. If testing heavy loads, we should either increase their quota for the POC or recommend Dedicated trial to remove throttling.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: new canary config applied to hosted cluster for route `api.redwood.example.com` at 1913123550 by ryan-se
nina-sre: For troubleshooting, please ask them to provide:
- output of `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` from within their VPC
- `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts`
- any proxy config that does TLS inspection (vendor + version)
jenna-sales: I'll request those now and offer the temporary public hostname option. Also asking if they'd accept a short call with infra to screenshare.
arthur-infra: If they give pcap we can confirm SNI and whether a downstream cert replacement occurs. If SNI is rewritten we can propose using a customer-allowed hostname we control (e.g., ppc-redwood-{id}.customer.example) — but that requires DNS delegation which eats time.
ryan-se: Quick note for the runbook I'll paste into the thread and send to customer:
ryan-se: ```
1) Confirm Private DNS resolves to interface endpoint IPs
2) Ensure security group allows 443 from your NAT and proxy IP ranges
3) If TLS inspection is present, allow passthrough for api.redwood.example.com or exempt from MITM
4) If testing load, request a temporary quota bump from us (cc: @mark-sales)
5) If unwilling to change proxy behavior, request a short-lived public-hostname POC (tradeoff: not private)
```
jenna-sales: Thanks all — pinging customer with runbook now. Will update here after we get dig / openssl outputs.
jenna-sales: quick follow — they shared `dig +short` and it returned `10.0.9.22`. openssl shows cert subject CN=proxy.corp.internal
nina-sre: that's a clear MITM. Recommend either exempting the hostname in the proxy or using the public-hostname POC. I'll prepare a one-pager on the security implications for their SOC review.
mark-sales: I'll draft a short pricing addendum for the Dedicated POC option (24/7 throughput + dedicated IPs) and attach it to the SOW. Expect draft in ~1h.
jenna-sales: perfect. setting up call with their infra for 14:30 PT. thanks everyone :pray:
